_preset: FAN SEARCH -- seed configs, then one round of mutations. Two generations, no selection pressure: generation 0 evaluates each seed config unchanged, generation 1 fans every seed out into children. Use it to explore the neighbourhood of configs you already like, or to sample fresh rules from an all-zero seed. For a real multi-generation hill-climb, use search.json instead.
_generations: 2 = seeds (gen 0) + one round of children (gen 1). This is the minimum that produces mutations at all; 1 would only score the seeds.
_beam_width: Set high enough that EVERY seed survives generation 0 and gets to breed. The beam is capped at min(seeds scored, beam_width), so a small beam here would silently drop the worst-scoring seeds before they fan out.
_children_per_parent: How wide each seed fans. Total candidates = seeds + (seeds x this) + immigrants.
_mutation_scale: How far children stray from their seed. Measured L2 from the parent rule: 0.19 / 0.38 / 1.34 / 3.82 at scale 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.35 / 1.0. IGNORED when a seed's rule is all zeros -- see _zero_rule_note.
_zero_rule_note: An all-zero rule is the engine's 'no behaviour authored' sentinel: the shader generates a rule from mutation_seed instead of reading one, and generated rules are never mutated. So on such a seed, mutation_scale does nothing (pinned to 0) and each child is an INDEPENDENT random rule rather than a small step -- measured L2 between them is 8-12, where authored siblings at scale 0.15 sit near 0.75. Selecting the particle writes the generated rule in as a real one, so the children themselves are normal population members and can be mutated properly afterwards. Rows produced this way carry extra.from_zero_rule in the manifest.
_seed_configs: The configs to fan out from. Paths are relative to the repo root. An empty list falls back to random immigrants, which makes this a pure random sampling run.
_objective: PICK ONE: reference_dir OR caption. Setting both is a config error. Keys starting with _ are ignored by the loader (JSON has no comments).
